Section 1: Figure description
This figure compares two different methods, ERM and mixup, in a visual representation. The ERM method is depicted on the left, showing a clear separation between the orange and green points. The mixup method on the right shows a more blended distribution of the orange and green points.

Section 2: Text in figure
ERM
mixup

Section 1: Figure description
This figure is a line graph comparing the percentage of misses for two methods, ERM and mixup, across different values of lambda (λ). The x-axis represents lambda values ranging from 0.00 to 1.00, while the y-axis shows the percentage of misses, ranging from 0 to 50. The ERM method is represented by the blue line, and the mixup method is represented by the orange line.

Section 2: Figure details
The figure shows that the ERM method has a higher percentage of misses compared to the mixup method. The ERM method reaches its peak at around 0.50 lambda, with a percentage of misses slightly above 20. The mixup method has a lower percentage of misses, with its peak at around 0.75 lambda, with a percentage of misses slightly above 10. Both methods have a similar percentage of misses at 0.00 and 1.00 lambda, which is close to 0.

Description: The figure is a line graph comparing two series, ERM and mixup, over a range of λ values from 0.00 to 1.00. The y-axis represents the norm of the gradient ∥∇ℓ∥, ranging from 0.0 to 0.5. The ERM series peaks at around 0.2, while the mixup series remains relatively flat throughout the range.

Description: The figure is a line graph showing the CIFAR-10 Test Error over epochs for two models: DenseNet-190 baseline and DenseNet-190 mixup. The DenseNet-190 baseline starts with a high error rate, which decreases rapidly over the first 50 epochs, then stabilizes around 5. The DenseNet-190 mixup also starts high but decreases more gradually, stabilizing at a slightly higher error rate of around 6.

description:
## Figure Description
This figure displays a comparison between two types of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs): the standard ERM GAN and the mixup GAN with a mixing parameter α = 0.2. It shows the effect of mixup on stabilizing GAN training over iterations 10, 100, 1000, 10000, and 20000. The figure consists of two main sections, each containing five plots representing the distribution of generated data points at different training stages.
